title: Weight Going Up Before Your Period: Is It Normal?
intro: Yes, it's very normal, and it's mostly water, not fat. Many women see their weight go up by an estimated 0.5-2 kg a few days before their period, then come back down after their period starts.

sections.h: Why weight goes up before your period
sections.p: Hormone changes before your period can make your body hold more water. Your stomach also bloats easily and your bowel movements slow down. All this adds to the number on the scale, even though your fat hasn't increased within a few days.

sections.h: Cravings are real, not a lack of willpower
sections.p: Many feel hungrier and crave sweet or salty food before their period. Don't fight it all the way until you end up overeating. Give yourself planned room, for example a small piece of chocolate, 2-3 dates or fruit. Make sure your main meals have protein so you stay fuller.

Some days you have energy, some days your body feels heavy. On tiring days, a 20-30 minute walk or light stretching is already good. No need to force a heavy session if you have period cramps. What matters is that you keep moving consistently throughout the month.

sections.h: How to read the scale properly
sections.p: Don't compare your weight the week before your period with the week after. Instead, compare it with the same phase last month. You can also record your waist measurement and see how your clothes fit. This gives a calmer and more honest picture.

If your periods are irregular, very heavy, very painful, or your weight keeps going up for no reason, see a doctor for a check-up. Conditions like PCOS or thyroid problems need to be assessed by a doctor. If your period is late and there's a chance you're pregnant, do a pregnancy test first.

action: Mark your period dates in your phone calendar and watch your weight pattern for 2-3 months.
Drink enough plain water and cut down on very salty food like instant noodles and keropok in the week before your period.
Keep planned snacks like fruit or dates at your desk so cravings don't turn into finishing all the meeting kuih.
On tiring days, do a 20-minute walk instead of a heavy workout.
Compare your weight with the same phase last month, not with last week.
myth: Many assume gaining 2 kg the week before their period means they've gained fat and their effort has failed. In reality, such a short-term increase is mostly water and bloating, and it usually goes down after your period.

faq.q: How long does this water weight usually stay?
faq.a: For many women, it starts going up a few days before the period and comes down within a few days after the period starts. Everyone's pattern is different, which is why it's good to track your own for a few months.

faq.q: Should I stop weighing myself when my period is coming?
faq.a: You can, if the number stresses you out. Or keep weighing but treat it as data only. Focus on your monthly average and waist measurement.

faq.q: Can I eat chocolate when I have cravings?
faq.a: Yes. Take a small portion, enjoy it slowly, and don't eat straight from a big pack. Foods like chocolate can fit into your eating, what matters is quantity and frequency.
